  Terse gloss: "Surpassing degree, excess, extraordinary measure; used by Paul to express what goes beyond all normal scale."
  Readable gloss: "A noun denoting something that exceeds normal limits—an extraordinary degree or surplus. Paul uses it almost exclusively, often in the frozen phrase 'kath' hyperbolen' (beyond measure, exceedingly). He speaks of sin becoming 'sinful beyond measure' (Rom 7:13), of affliction in Asia that was 'beyond measure, beyond strength' (2 Cor 1:8), and most strikingly of an 'eternal weight of glory beyond all comparison' (2 Cor 4:17). English borrowed this word directly as 'hyperbole,' but in Paul's hands it is no rhetorical exaggeration—it describes realities that genuinely surpass human categories."
